question.problem: Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=2{e}^{3\theta }$ for $-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=2{e}^{3\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=6{e}^{3\theta }.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{(2{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}+{(6{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{4{e}^{6\theta }+36{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{40{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\sqrt{10}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{e}^{3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{10}}{3}{e}^{3\theta }{|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{10}}{3}({e}^{3\pi /2}-{e}^{-3\pi /2}).\end{aligned}
$$
